The skill `officeqa-treasury-bulletin` now has a new section "Vessel-tonnage / navigation-of-commerce tables (net registered tonnage by flag)" capturing the two generalizable lessons from this miss:

1. **Pooled aggregate share, not a difference.** "What percentage of total X in Jan, Feb, Mar was attributed to American vessels" = sum(component over 3 months) / sum(total over 3 months) × 100 ≈ 34.4. My 5.3 came from treating it as a between-month difference.

2. **Trap wording.** The phrase "the single percentage point difference" is a red herring — the gold value is still the aggregate share, not a subtraction. The strong diagnostic: my Pearson r (0.391) matched gold exactly, proving I read the right two series; the first value being ~6x too small therefore had to be a computation/wording error, not a data-read error.

3. **New table type documented:** early-Bulletin navigation/commerce tonnage tables with American / Foreign / Total(grand) flag rows, American flag a ~30-40% minority in 1941, "grand total" = all-flags Total not the Foreign row.

Memory is at its 2,200-char cap, so I couldn't add a mirror note there, but the skill is the durable home for this procedure and a future agent loading it will get the full fix.
